artifacts.summary: 3-phase plan (1.75h) giving a concrete-path overlap precedence over the reserved __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel when the same task pair overlaps on both, pinned by a new order-independence fixture; re-scoped after the dispatch's stated deliverable was measured already met.

user_decision.question: This record's stated deliverable (making WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH go green) is already satisfied in live code -- the fixture passes today and the whole_tree_claim branch already emits all asserted fields. The only measurably-unmet requirement is the description's own REGRESSION clause (a concrete-path collision between two sentinel-declaring tasks is masked as a bare whole-tree claim, order-dependently). Proceed against that clause, or close the record as already-satisfied?
options: Proceed with the plan as written -- close the order-dependent concrete-path masking, the one requirement in the description that live state does not already meet
Close the record as already-satisfied with no code change, and file the masking as its own record
user_decision.recommended: Proceed with the plan as written -- close the order-dependent concrete-path masking, the one requirement in the description that live state does not already meet
user_decision.obligation: The description's REGRESSION clause: two sentinel-declaring tasks whose concrete paths genuinely intersect must still report the concrete overlapping path rather than being relabelled as a bare whole-tree claim. Checkable against the plan's Phase 2 verification: both declaration orderings of a sentinel-plus-shared-concrete-path pair must yield defer_reason file_scope_collision with overlapping_path naming the concrete path and no claim_sentinel field, while WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH stays green with its assertions byte-identical.

memory_candidates.content: A comparator that RELABELS one already-selected hit into a different, more specific verdict shape (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh relabeling a scopes_overlap_first hit on the reserved __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel into defer_reason whole_tree_claim) inherits a masking hazard from the underlying predicate's first-match-wins return: when a task pair overlaps on BOTH the special token and a real path, which label fires depends on the ARRAY DECLARATION ORDER of the declared file_scope entries, not on which finding is stronger. The general fix is a precedence wrapper composed from the existing predicate (compare with the special token filtered out first; fall back to the unfiltered call only when that yields nothing), never a change to the predicate itself -- which keeps every other consumer of the shared comparator byte-identical. The masking is not merely cosmetic: in this case file_scope_collision carries a consumer-side --allow-scope-collision override (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, cross_batch only) that whole_tree_claim does not, so the relabel silently removes an operator remedy.
